rows.citation: Kassem, M., Ribeiro, F., Nadi, S. (2026). An Automated Methodology for Generating Labeled Datasets of Semantic Errors in Code. Proceedings of the 3rd International Workshop on Large Language Models For Code (LLM4Code '26), ACM, pp. 14-20.
rows.model_type: general software: Python functions from HumanEval and BigCodeBench (LLM-generated-code error study)
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - GPT-4.1 injects single, isolated semantic bugs into correct code following an established error taxonomy, yielding labelled faulty variants.
rows.multiple_stimuli: unclear - abstract does not say how behavioural change of each seeded bug is confirmed; full text blocked (ACM DL returned a bot page).
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - general Python code; no neural simulation or feature extraction.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no selection of test inputs or test suites described in the abstract.
rows.heldout_evaluation: unclear - output is a dataset intended for classifier research; no held-out evaluation described in abstract.
rows.ai_transformations: yes - an LLM (GPT-4.1) is the fault-injection mechanism, motivated by subtle semantic errors in LLM-generated code.
rows.software: none verified (a labelled Python dataset artifact is described; its location could not be verified because the full text was inaccessible)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shares only the single-fault seeding principle. NeuroSem would use recorded rule-based operators on NeuroML models, classify equivalence by simulation, and select stimulation protocols for detection.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (title, authors, venue, pages, date; no abstract); OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar APIs (abstract, CC-BY open-access status, DBLP key conf/llm4code/KassemRN26). ACM DL PDF and DBLP search returned bot-challenge pages.
rows.found_via: Crossref silent semantic errors LLM code query; verified via Crossref (no abstract)

rows.citation: Xu, Y., Yang, J., Chen, T.-H. (P.) (2026). SWE-Refactor: A Repository-Level Benchmark for Real-World LLM-Based Code Refactoring. arXiv preprint arXiv:2602.03712.
rows.model_type: general software: 18 Java projects, method-level developer refactorings (atomic and compound)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - mines 1,099 developer-written behaviour-preserving refactorings; no fault seeding.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - behaviour preservation checked with compilation, project test suites and coverage data; not a designed stimulus battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - Java source code; checks are test pass rates, AST refactoring detection and CodeBLEU.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - relies on existing project tests; no test or input selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - fixed benchmark used to evaluate nine LLMs and an agent; no discovery/held-out split for a tuned method.
rows.ai_transformations: yes - LLMs and a Codex agent perform refactorings, verified by compilation, tests and RefactoringMiner.
rows.software: SWE-Refactor benchmark - v1 appendix states it is 'to be released'; no public URL verified
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Parallels NeuroSem valid transformations, but trusts existing unit tests plus AST detection in Java. NeuroSem checks simulated neuronal behaviour across a calibrated stimulus battery, adds seeded faults and protocol selection.
rows.verification_method: DataCite DOI API (title, abstract, dates); arXiv abs page (creator meta tags split the third name, but the displayed author list reads 'Tse-Hsun (Peter) Chen', resolving it); arXiv HTML full text v1 (methods, hosting appendix).
rows.found_via: DataCite (arXiv DOIs) LLM + refactoring title query; abstract via DataCite

rows.citation: Aygün, E., Belyaeva, A., Comanici, G., et al. (2026). An AI system to help scientists write expert-level empirical software. Nature, 654, 909-916.
rows.model_type: general empirical scientific software with scorable metrics (single-cell analysis, COVID-19 forecasting, geospatial, zebrafish neural-activity prediction, numerical integrals)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - generates and rewrites candidate programs to raise a quality metric; no seeded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - each candidate program is scored against a task quality metric, not probed with a battery of perturbation inputs.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - includes a zebrafish neural-activity prediction task, but no electrophysiological features of simulated neuron models.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - tree search optimises code solutions, not test or stimulus selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - solutions compared on public leaderboards and forecasting benchmarks; per-task split details not reviewed here.
rows.ai_transformations: yes - LLM plus Flat UCB tree search generates, executes and scores program variants.
rows.software: ERA reference implementation https://github.com/google-research/era (LICENSE file: Apache License)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: ERA optimises code for a target metric; NeuroSem instead tests whether edits to neuron models silently change behaviour under untargeted stimuli, a complementary safeguard. No overlap with core method.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (metadata, abstract, volume/pages, preprint relation); nature.com article page (code availability statement); GitHub raw README and LICENSE.
rows.found_via: Europe PMC LLM generated code silent/subtle errors query; verified via Crossref + abstract

rows.citation: Chen, Y. T., Hicks, S. C. (2026). Mind the alignment gap: a spatial transcriptomics benchmark for scientific coding agents. bioRxiv (openRxiv) preprint.
rows.model_type: spatial transcriptomics tissue-slice alignment tasks (40 tasks from SABench) posed to coding agents
rows.controlled_mutations: no - varies agent prompt and environment configuration, not seeded model faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - tasks scored by one hidden alignment metric; no behavioural perturbation battery.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no test or protocol selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: yes - agents see public inputs and output schema; labels, gold coordinates, metric definitions and scorer are hidden, same scorer for all runs.
rows.ai_transformations: yes - coding agents in three configurations across 120 runs; trace inspection reports unnecessary transformations and fragile workflows.
rows.software: Gen2Bench https://github.com/yiqunchen/Gen2Bench cited in full text; returned HTTP 404 on 2026-09-13 (not publicly accessible)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Informs design of NeuroSem's optional isolated agent study (hidden scorer, fixed configurations, trace audit); has no neuron models, mutants, tolerances or protocol selection.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (metadata, abstract, publisher openRxiv); Europe PMC REST search (PPR1276292); bioRxiv details API (authors Chen, Y. T.; Hicks, S. C.; CC-BY); bioRxiv JATS full text (methods, code link); GitHub page check.
rows.found_via: Crossref SciCode benchmark query; verified via Crossref + Europe PMC abstract

rows.citation: Siegel, Z. S., Kapoor, S., Nadgir, N., et al. (2024). CORE-Bench: Fostering the Credibility of Published Research Through a Computational Reproducibility Agent Benchmark. arXiv preprint arXiv:2409.11363.
rows.model_type: general computational research code (270 tasks from 90 CodeOcean capsules in computer science, social science, medicine; Python or R)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - agents reproduce unmodified published code; no seeded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - tasks ask questions about outputs of running each paper's code; no perturbation battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - task answers are reported study results, not neural features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no test or input selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: yes - train/test task split with encrypted test set; answers judged within 95% prediction intervals from three manual reruns.
rows.ai_transformations: partial - AutoGPT and CORE-Agent (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini) set up and run code; they reproduce rather than edit models.
rows.software: CORE-Bench harness https://github.com/siegelz/core-bench (LICENSE: MIT; README says no longer actively maintained, recommends HAL harness); dataset https://huggingface.co/datasets/siegelz/core-bench
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Hidden-answer scoring with rerun-based tolerance is a precedent for NeuroSem's agent-study scoring; NeuroSem derives tolerances from numerical refinement and targets behavioural drift from model edits, not reproduction.
rows.verification_method: DataCite DOI API (metadata, abstract, v1/v2 dates); arXiv abs page (authors, code link); arXiv HTML full text (evaluation criteria); GitHub raw README and LICENSE (REST API was rate-limited).
rows.found_via: DataCite (arXiv DOIs) agents + reproduction query; abstract via DataCite

rows.citation: Huang, Z., Cao, Y., Shargh, A. K., et al. (2026). Can Coding Agents Reproduce Findings in Computational Materials Science? arXiv preprint arXiv:2605.00803.
rows.model_type: computational materials science simulation workflows (DFT, molecular dynamics, discrete dislocation dynamics, statistical/ML methods)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - agents reconstruct and execute published workflows; no seeded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - each claim requires one reconstructed end-to-end workflow; no stimulus battery.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no test or protocol selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - expert-curated claims in a gated dataset, scored by an LLM rubric evaluator audited against experts; no discovery/held-out split.
rows.ai_transformations: yes - evaluates Claude Code, Codex CLI and a multi-phase agent reproducing simulation-based claims, with failure-mode analysis.
rows.software: AutoMat https://github.com/JHU-CLSP/AutoMat (LICENSE: MIT); gated dataset https://hf.co/datasets/jhu-clsp/AutoMat
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Agent reproduction of simulation claims in another domain with LLM-judged scoring; NeuroSem's agent study would score agent edits to neuron models with deterministic hidden stimulus tests.
rows.verification_method: DataCite DOI API (metadata, abstract); arXiv abs page (authors, v1/v2 history, comment 'COLM 2026' is author-reported and not independently verified); arXiv HTML full text; GitHub raw README and LICENSE.
rows.found_via: DataCite (arXiv DOIs) agents + reproduction query; abstract via DataCite
